author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Keep PS2 regions and revisions separate in EmuCoreX
summary: Identify PAL, NTSC-U, NTSC-J, and revision-specific working images by serial, hash, video standard, and save compatibility so covers, profiles, patches, and memory-card tests never cross the wrong executable.
heroAlt: Media Preservation Frontend media-information screen showing disc fields used to distinguish regional PS2 releases

blocks.text: Start with serial and executable identity

Regional releases can change language, frame cadence, censorship, executable layout, patches, and save product codes. Even two discs from one region can be different revisions. A library label such as Game (USA) is useful only when it rests on verified disc evidence. Record serial, region, revision clues, image bytes, and SHA-256 before creating names or profiles.
Never apply a PNACH, widescreen fix, compatibility profile, or memory-card workaround to another region merely because the title screen looks the same. CRC and serial scope matter.
Create an identity row for each owned release

items: Independent verified dump for every physical regional or revision disc.
Disc label and dump log available for comparison.
Detected serial recorded from a clean cold boot.
No inherited per-game profile on the first identity run.
Separate native save test card or backed-up memory card.
1. Place each working image in a stable library folder without renaming it over another edition.
2. Cold-boot at safe defaults and record the serial, displayed language, video cadence, and any revision text.
3. Name the working copy with title, region, serial, and revision only after those fields agree.
4. Refresh EmuCoreX and verify that each edition resolves to a distinct path and identity.
5. Create a per-game profile only for the edition that demonstrated a need; include the serial in the test note.
6. Test a fresh native save on each edition before attempting to share an older save.
7. Keep patches and texture packs separated by their documented serial or hash scope.

blocks.text: A PAL image may target 50 Hz timing while an NTSC image targets roughly 60 Hz, but individual games can offer modes that complicate simple labels. Judge the actual release and executable. Save compatibility is also a game decision; never modify a valuable card to discover it without a backup.
Evidence that editions are not being conflated
Every edition needs its own chain from physical disc to active profile.

items: Hash and serial records point to one exact working image.
Region and revision appear in the filename or private manifest.
Each EmuCoreX entry opens the expected language and cadence.
Per-game fixes name the edition they were tested on.
A memory-card test does not overwrite the only copy of progress.

blocks.text: Signs that regional identity was assumed

items: A patch has no effect or corrupts startup: executable CRC does not match.
The game reports no save despite a visible card: product code or region differs.
Two editions share one profile and only one renders correctly: separate their settings.
A cover or title is wrong but serial is correct: fix metadata without replacing image bytes.

blocks.text: Return each edition to an isolated baseline

Disable copied patches, remove shared per-game overrides, and restore the backed-up card. Cold-boot each verified image at Safe defaults, rename only from the identity ledger, and rebuild edition-specific profiles one at a time.
Marketing regions are not executable revisions

USA, Europe, and Japan labels are broad. Greatest Hits, Platinum, language reprints, and later pressings can contain changed executables under the same market name. Preserve revision evidence rather than collapsing everything into three folders.
